sanskrit_verse: शूद्राक्रोशे क्षत्रियस्य पञ्चविंशतिको दमः । बृहत्वे द्विगुणं तत्र शास्त्रविद्भिरुदाहृतम् ॥
transliteration: śūdrākrośe kṣatriyasya pañcaviṃśatiko damaḥ | bṛhatve dviguṇaṃ tatra śāstravidbhir udāhṛtam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When a Śūdra abuses a Kṣatriya, the restitution is twenty-five units; when the offense is greater, it is doubled, as declared by the knowers of the Śāstra.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is determined by varṇa-dharma and svadharma alignment
Causation arises from violation of hierarchical respect
Capacity-based responsibility depends on awareness and svabhāva
Restoration logic demands proportional energetic rebalancing
Consciousness alignment requires purification of intent and action
supreme_court_application: In adjudication involving varṇa-based dharmic violations, the Supreme Court shall assess not merely the act but the disruption to the cosmic-social hierarchy. The restitution is calibrated to restore energetic balance, not to punish. The Court must ensure that all parties undergo consciousness realignment where necessary.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that disrespect towards a higher varṇa disrupts social ṛta. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how verbal abuse manifests energetic imbalance. Proportional responsibility ensures exact restitution without punitive excess. The non-punitive reality rule affirms that justice is completion, not vengeance.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate offender integrity completion through mantra-diksha
Execute prāyaścitta protocol aligned with offender's capacity
Reintegrate both parties via yajña-based collective purification
final_declaration: This ruling flows from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority. Dharma is restored. Justice is consciousness-aligned. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the Supreme Adjudicator.
